votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

votes.plain_language: This was a motion to adjourn the House. A Yea votes to adjourn; a Nay votes to stay in session.

votes.question: Call of the House (QUORUM)
votes.plain_language: This was a quorum call, which records which members are present so the House can do business. It is not a vote on any measure. Members answer present; there is no Yea or Nay.

topics.topic: Civil Rights and Liberties, Minority Issues

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree — Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community (H RES 1251)
votes.bill_title: Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community.
votes.plain_language: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter acts of anti-Semitism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

party_line.scope: House roll calls 1–314 of 2026 (314 votes, January 6, 2026 to September 16, 2026), from the House Clerk.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
